change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The required torque controller response time for accelerator pedal demand above 70% was reduced from 100 ms to 80 ms. Verification must update script limits to 80 ms and re-test positive torque latency.

assessments.reason: The test directly verifies VCU-DR-01 response time for 75% pedal step. The tightened threshold of 80 ms invalidates both the previous PASS result of 94 ms and the 100 ms script limit.
evidence: Procedure: Step validated accelerator demand to 75%; confirm requested positive torque no later than 100 ms
assessments.recommended_action: Update test script threshold to 80 ms and re-execute the test against the new software build.

assessments.reason: The test exercises 85% pedal demand and is linked to VCU-DR-01, but response timing was not recorded in the previous test execution. Existing evidence is insufficient to confirm compliance with the new 80 ms limit.
evidence: Procedure: Apply 85% pedal with emergency-brake input
Comment: Timing not reported in old evidence
assessments.recommended_action: Re-run the arbitration test with response timing measurement enabled to verify torque issuance within 80 ms.

assessments.reason: The test procedure evaluates torque response latency for 75-95% pedal sweeps, which directly tests VCU-DR-01 functionality despite a missing requirement link. The previous result of 92 ms and legacy tolerance of 95 ms fail the new 80 ms limit.
evidence: Procedure: Sweep demand 75–95% at nominal and high-load cases; recorded maximum 92 ms
Comment: Legacy suite still checks 95 ms tolerance
Workshop note: High-load campaign did not keep all requirement hyperlinks after migration
assessments.recommended_action: Restore requirement link to VCU-DR-01, update test tolerance to 80 ms, and re-test under high load.

assessments.reason: This test measures brake actuator command latency under VCU-BRK-03. Workshop notes explicitly state that brake command latency uses a different measurement clock and must not be conflated with positive torque response timing.
evidence: Workshop note: Brake command latency and positive torque command latency are measured by different clocks. The two values should not be conflated.
assessments.recommended_action: No action required; retain existing test procedure for VCU-BRK-03.

assessments.reason: The test checks sensor degradation handling and fault logging when wheel-speed input is disconnected, verifying VCU-DGN-04. It does not exercise driver pedal torque response.
evidence: Procedure: Unplug simulated wheel-speed sensor and confirm degraded mode + fault log

assessments.reason: The test validates audit logging of mode changes under VCU-LOG-05 and is unrelated to torque response latency.
evidence: Procedure: Change Comfort to Sport; log timestamp and build identifier

assessments.reason: The test reference link is TBD, ownership is unclarified, and the test was NOT RUN. While 80% pedal demand is used, available text does not clarify whether latency or steady-state response is evaluated.
evidence: Comment: Ownership and source link to be clarified
Procedure: At 80% pedal and elevated load, check that torque delivery is consistent...
assessments.recommended_action: Resolve TBD requirement link with systems engineering, assign test owner, and define whether latency timing applies.

assessments.reason: The test is linked to an unknown legacy requirement VCU-OLD-88, causing broken traceability. Relevance to the revised VCU-DR-01 cannot be determined without engineering input.
evidence: Comment: Imported row; requirements catalog changed
assessments.recommended_action: Review legacy requirement mapping with systems engineering to re-link or archive the test.

assessments.reason: The test verifies mode-dependent torque ramp profiles under VCU-MOD-06. It contains no quantitative response-time assertion related to VCU-DR-01.
The test verifies pedal input signal filtering for short spikes under VCU-DR-02. It tests signal rejection rather than valid driver torque command latency.
evidence: Procedure: Inject 7 ms false pedal pulse and verify no propagated torque request

assessments.reason: The test checks emergency brake override priority over propulsion torque under VCU-BRK-03. It evaluates torque suppression rather than driver pedal response timing.
evidence: Procedure: While demand is high, request emergency braking and verify positive torque drops according to brake priority

assessments.reason: The test measures ECU power-up startup timing against a 500 ms limit. Although the requirement link is missing, test content confirms it is unrelated to accelerator pedal response.
evidence: Procedure: Power cycle the ECU; verify readiness within 500 ms
assessments.recommended_action: Link test to the appropriate platform startup requirement; no change required for VCU-DR-01.
